abstract: Climate change is a massive multidimensional shift. Temperature shifts, in particular, have important implications for urbanization, agriculture, health, productivity, and poverty, among other things. While much research has documented rising mean temperature levels, the authors also examine range-based measures of daily temperature volatility. Specifically, using data for select US cities over the past half-century, the authors compare the evolving time series dynamics of the average daily temperature (AVG) and the diurnal temperature range (DTR; the difference between the daily maximum and minimum temperatures). The authors characterize trend and seasonality in these two series using linear models with time-varying coefficients. These straightforward yet flexible approximations provide evidence of evolving DTR seasonality and stable AVG seasonality.
abstract_zh: 气候变化是一场巨大的多维度转变。气温变化尤其对城市化、农业、健康、生产率以及贫困等诸多方面具有重要影响。尽管已有大量研究记录了平均气温水平的上升，作者还考察了基于日内极差的日气温波动度量。具体而言，利用过去半个世纪部分美国城市的数据，作者比较了日均气温（AVG）与日温差（DTR，即每日最高与最低气温之差）两个序列随时间演变的动态特征。作者使用具有时变系数的线性模型刻画了这两个序列的趋势与季节性。这些简洁而灵活的近似方法表明，日温差的季节性在演变，而日均气温的季节性保持稳定。

title: Probability Assessments of an Ice-Free Arctic: Comparing Statistical and Climate Model Projections
abstract: The downward trend in the amount of Arctic sea ice is a key factor determining the pace and intensity of future global climate change. Diminished sea ice also has a wide range of other environmental and economic consequences. Based on several decades of satellite data, we provide statistical forecasts of Arctic sea ice extent during the rest of this century. The best fitting statistical model indicates that overall sea ice coverage is declining at an increasing rate. By contrast, average projections from the CMIP5 global climate models foresee a gradual slowing of Arctic sea ice loss even in scenarios with high carbon emissions. Our long-range statistical projections also deliver probability assessments of the timing of an ice-free Arctic. These results indicate almost a 60 percent chance of an effectively ice-free Arctic Ocean during some summer in the 2030s -- much earlier than the average projection from global climate models.
abstract_zh: 北极海冰面积的下降趋势是决定未来全球气候变化速度与强度的关键因素。海冰减少还会带来广泛的其他环境和经济后果。基于数十年的卫星数据，我们对本世纪剩余时间内北极海冰范围做出了统计预测。最佳拟合的统计模型表明，海冰总覆盖面积正以加速的速度减少。相比之下，CMIP5全球气候模式的平均预测认为，即便在高碳排放情景下，北极海冰损失也将逐渐放缓。我们的长期统计预测还给出了北极无冰时间的概率评估。这些结果表明，北极海洋在2030年代的某个夏季实现实际无冰状态的概率接近60%——远早于全球气候模式的平均预测。

abstract: Understanding the dynamic evolution of the yield curve is critical to many financial tasks, including pricing financial assets and their derivatives, managing financial risk, allocating portfolios, structuring fiscal debt, conducting monetary policy, and valuing capital goods. Unfortunately, most yield curve models tend to be theoretically rigorous but empirically disappointing, or empirically successful but theoretically lacking. Against that background, we propose two extensions of the classic yield curve model of Nelson and Siegel that are both theoretically rigorous and empirically successful. The first extension is the dynamic Nelson-Siegel model (DNS), while the second takes this dynamic version and makes it arbitrage-free (AFNS). We emphasize both descriptive and efficient-markets aspects, we pay special attention to the links between the yield curve and macroeconomic fundamentals, and we show why DNS and AFNS are likely to remain of lasting appeal even as alternative arbitrage-free models are developed.

abstract: On the successes and failures of various parts of modern financial risk management, emphasizing the known (K), the unknown (u) and the unknowable (U). We illustrate a KuU-based perspective for conceptualizing financial risks and designing effective risk management strategies. Sometimes we focus on K, and sometimes on U, but most often our concerns blend aspects of K and u and U. Indeed K and U are extremes of a smooth spectrum, with many of the most interesting and relevant situations interior. Statistical issues emerge as central to risk measurement, and we push toward additional progress. But economic issues of incentives and strategic behavior emerge as central for risk management, as we illustrate in a variety of contexts.

title: Weather Forecasting for Weather Derivatives
venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association
abstract: Weather derivatives are a fascinating new type of Arrow-Debreu security, making pre-specified payouts if pre-specified weather events occur, and the market for such derivatives has grown rapidly. Weather modeling and forecasting are crucial to both the demand and supply sides of the weather derivatives market. On the demand side, to assess the potential for hedging against weather surprises and to formulate the appropriate hedging strategies, one needs to determine how much "weather noise" exists for weather derivatives to eliminate, and that requires weather modeling and forecasting. On the supply side, standard approaches to arbitrage-free pricing are irrelevant in weather derivative contexts, and so the only way to price options reliably is again by modeling and forecasting the underlying weather variable. Curiously, however, little thought has been given to the crucial question of how best to approach weather modeling and forecasting in the context of weather derivative demand and supply. The vast majority of extant weather forecasting literature has a structural "atmospheric science" feel, and although such an approach may be best for forecasting six hours ahead, it is not obvious that it is best for the longer horizons relevant for weather derivatives, such as six days, six weeks, or six months. In particular, good forecasting does not necessarily require a structural model. In this paper, then, we take a seemingly-naive nonstructural time-series approach to modeling and forecasting daily average temperature in ten U.S. cities, and we inquire systematically as to whether it proves useful. The answer is, perhaps surprisingly, yes. Time series modeling reveals a wealth of information about both conditional mean dynamics and the conditional variance dynamics of average daily temperature, some of which seems not to have been noticed previously, and it provides similarly sharp insights into both the distributions of weather and the distributions of weather surprises, and the key differences between them. The success of time-series modeling in capturing conditional mean dynamics translates into successful point forecasting, a fact which, together with the success of time-series modeling in identifying and characterizing the distributions of weather surprises, translates as well into successful density forecasting.
abstract_zh: 天气衍生品是一种引人入胜的新型Arrow-Debreu证券，在预先设定的天气事件发生时支付预先设定的收益，该市场近年来迅速增长。天气建模与预测对天气衍生品市场的需求端和供给端都至关重要。在需求端，要评估对天气意外进行对冲的潜力并制定适当的对冲策略，就需要确定天气衍生品能够消除的“天气噪声”有多大，而这需要天气建模与预测。在供给端，标准的无套利定价方法在天气衍生品的语境下并不适用，因此可靠地为期权定价的唯一途径，同样是对基础天气变量进行建模与预测。然而奇怪的是，对于如何在天气衍生品的供需背景下最好地进行天气建模与预测这一关键问题，人们很少加以思考。现有的绝大多数天气预报文献带有明显的结构性“大气科学”色彩；尽管这种方法或许最适合预测六小时之后的天气，但对于天气衍生品所关注的更长时间跨度（如六天、六周或六个月），它未必是最佳选择。具体而言，良好的预测并不一定需要结构性模型。因此，本文采用一种看似朴素的非结构性时间序列方法，对美国十个城市的日平均气温进行建模与预测，并系统地检验该方法是否有用。答案出人意料地是肯定的。时间序列建模揭示了日平均气温条件均值动态与条件方差动态的大量信息，其中一些以前似乎未被注意到；它同样为天气分布及天气意外分布，以及二者之间的关键差异，提供了敏锐的洞见。时间序列建模在捕捉条件均值动态方面的成功，转化为成功的点预测；而时间序列建模在识别和刻画天气意外分布方面的成功，又与之一道，转化为成功的密度预测。

Why are Estimates of Agricultural Supply Response so Variable?
abstract: Estimates of the response of agricultural supply to movements in expected price display curiously large variation across crops, regions, and time periods. We argue that this anomoly may be traced, at least in part, to the statistical properties of the commonly-used econometric estimator, which has infinite moments of all orders and may have a bimodal distribution. We propose an alternative minimum- expected-loss estimator, establish its improved sampling properties, and argue for its usefulness in the empirical analysis of agricultural supply response.
abstract_zh: 农产品供给对预期价格变动的反应估计值，在不同作物、地区和时期之间表现出令人费解的巨大差异。我们认为，这一反常现象至少部分可归因于常用计量估计量的统计性质：该估计量具有所有阶的无限矩，并且可能呈双峰分布。我们提出了一种替代性的最小期望损失估计量，确立了其更优的抽样性质，并论证了其在农产品供给反应实证分析中的实用性。
